scope: Selected files and directories copied through the real Rust engine, private filesystem transactions and a Unix stream. No USB device, VM transfer channel or manager integration exercised.

verification.workflow_yaml: parsed; ARM64 and x86-64 copy-engine jobs configured, not yet executed in CI

debian_amd64.environment: Docker Desktop on macOS ARM64 with x86 emulation

covered: Selective directory tree copy, Unicode names, empty files/directories and payload larger than the 64 KiB buffer.
Actual Unix socket transfer and matching receiver receipt after syncing the private transaction.
Per-file SHA-256, manifest digest, size and entry limits, byte-count overflow and bounded headers.
Malformed version/header, unknown fields and entry types, duplicate/conflicting paths and absent parents.
Absolute paths, traversal, control/bidi characters, symlinks, hard links, FIFO and sockets rejected.
Existing transaction or symlink destination never reused or overwritten.
Opened source remains pinned when its pathname is replaced; changed source data aborts.
Corruption, truncation, invalid final marker and real connection cancellation remove partial transactions.
Receiver requires a private owned root; file/directory output modes verified.
limits: No authorization/capability issuer, expiry, transport deadlines or controller integration yet; these are mandatory caller responsibilities.
No real USB or inter-VM copy, device passthrough, import/export UI or chat delivery.
No ENOSPC, physical-memory OOM, power-loss or crash-recovery proof for the copy service yet.
The library does not enforce LUKS/tmpfs placement, mount flags or VM isolation; integration must supply them.
Tests use synthetic files in local temporary directories and disposable Docker layers; they do not prove absence of traces on the live USB.
Files are complete only under the receiver-private transaction; explicit release to the chat is still required.

initial_build_failure.reason: cargo fetch ran before an implicit library target existed in the Docker layer. Adding an explicit [lib] path fixed packaging; subsequent locked builds passed.
